title: High-throughput translational in vivo and ex vivo techniques for glioma molecular characterization -- eTumour consortium Kal1 subset [meningioma samples]

publications.title: Anosmin-1 contributes to brain tumor malignancy through integrin signal pathways.

platform: Affymetrix Human Genome U133 Plus 2.0 Array
processed_data_format: Array Data Files (per-sample .CEL-derived expression files) per the study's ArrayExpress FTP listing
needs_manual_review_reason: NEW RECORD (2026-07-16), closing out a coverage_gaps.md-carried lead: 'E-MTAB-1852 (glioma molecular characterization techniques) ... Not yet checked. Carried forward.' Despite the study's title and headline framing emphasizing glioma (the eTumour EU consortium's broader brain-tumor molecular-classification project), directly downloading and parsing the study's SDRF file (E-MTAB-1852.sdrf.txt, via https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/files/E-MTAB-1852/E-MTAB-1852.sdrf.txt -- the BioStudies REST API's JSON response for this study does not expose per-sample disease labels, only the SDRF does) found 15 rows with Characteristics[disease]='meningioma', all explicitly Characteristics[tumor grading]='WHO grade I', spanning 15 unique Characteristics[individual] values (et3096, et3159, et3170, et3265, et3271, et3272, et3297, et3298, et3302, et3308, et3309, et3859, et3860, et3861, et3863) with no replication (15 samples = 15 individuals). Per the study's own IDF, tumor typing was performed by 'a panel of independent pathologists across the etumour consortium' per WHO criteria on resected, snap-frozen tissue -- a real, primary, patient-tissue clinical cohort, not a secondary compilation (unlike a sibling coverage_gaps.md lead, E-MTAB-3732, checked the same session and found to be an unextractable secondary compiled meta-dataset -- see that entry in docs/coverage_gaps.md for why it was NOT added as a record). The IDF's own publication field listed 'Publication Status: under review' with no PMID, dated 2013 -- now over a decade stale; searched PubMed directly for the exact working title ('Kallmann syndrome-associated anosmin-1 contributes to brain tumor malignancy through integrin signal pathways') and found it was in fact published the following year under a slightly shortened title: 'Anosmin-1 contributes to brain tumor malignancy through integrin signal pathways' (Choy et al., Endocrine-Related Cancer 2014, PMID 24189182, DOI 10.1530/ERC-13-0181). Confirmed via its open-access PMC full text (PMC3869950) that it explicitly cites E-MTAB-1852 (1 occurrence, direct text search). Sole corresponding author (Soo-Hyun Kim) confirmed via the full text's own author-notes correspondence footnote ('Correspondence should be addressed to S-H Kim <skim@sgul.ac.uk>'), matching the IDF's IDF submitter institution (St George's University of London). No retraction/correction signal found. No per-sample sex/age/anatomic-location/brain-invasion/outcome data exists in the SDRF beyond disease and grade, so those fields correctly remain 'Not reported'. raw_data_available set false: only processed per-sample array data files are listed in the study's file listing, no raw .CEL files.
